e-4703.knowledge_point: Finding the Pivot Columns of a Matrix in Row Echelon Form
e-4703.problem:
The row echelon form matrix $B$ is given below. What are its pivot columns?

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & -3 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$
e-4703.worked_solution:
Remember that the pivots of a matrix in row echelon form are the first non-zero entries in each row of the matrix.

We can see that $B$ has $3$ pivots in the $2$nd, $3$rd, and $4$th columns:

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & -3 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

e-4704.knowledge_point: Finding the Non-Pivot Columns of a Matrix in Row Echelon Form
e-4704.problem:
The row echelon form matrix $C$ is given below. What are its **non**-pivot columns?

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$
e-4704.worked_solution:
Remember that the pivots of a matrix in row echelon form are the first non-zero entries in each row of the matrix.

We can see that $C$ has $3$ pivots in the $1$st, $3$rd, and $4$th columns:

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, the only non-pivot column is the $2$nd column.

e-4705.knowledge_point: Finding the Number of Pivot Columns of a Matrix
e-4705.problem:
Determine the number of pivot columns of the matrix $A,$ given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & -6 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$
e-4705.worked_solution:
First, we need to convert $A$ to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & -6 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Looking at the row echelon form, we see that $A$ has $3$ pivots, and therefore the number of pivot columns is $3.$

e-4706.knowledge_point: Finding the Pivot Columns of a Matrix
e-4706.problem:
What are the pivot columns of the matrix $B,$ given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -4 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$
e-4706.worked_solution:
First, we need to convert $B$ to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}B & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -4 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{4} & :={R}_{4}+(-\frac{2}{7}){R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & \end{aligned}
$$

Looking at the row echelon form, we see that $B$ has $3$ pivots. In particular, the pivot columns are the $1$st, $3$rd, and $4$th columns.

The row echelon form matrix $A$ is given below. What are the pivot columns of $A?$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 3 & -9 & 8 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & -4 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 7 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & -9\end{aligned}]
$$
content.worked_solution:
Remember that the pivots of a matrix in row echelon form are the first non-zero entries in each row of the matrix.

We can see that $A$ has $4$ pivots in the $2$nd, $3$rd, $4$th, and $5$th columns:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 3 & -9 & 8 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & -4 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 7 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & -9\end{aligned}]
$$

Remember that the pivots of a matrix in row echelon form are the first non-zero entries in each row of the matrix.

We can see that $B$ has $3$ pivots in the $1$st, $3$rd, and $4$th columns:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}3 & -8 & 0 & 4 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 7 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, the only non-pivot columns are the $2$nd and $5$th columns.

after.name: Question 11
after.problem:
Determine the number of pivot columns of the matrix $B,$ given by

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & -6 & 4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$
after.worked_solution:
First, we need to convert $B$ to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}B & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & -6 & 4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 6 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{4} & :={R}_{4}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 6 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Looking at the row echelon form, we see that $B$ has $3$ pivots, and therefore the number of pivot columns is $3.$

content.problem:
Determine the number of pivot columns of the matrix $C,$ given by

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 3 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & -3 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}].

$$

$$

Looking at the row echelon form, we see that $C$ has $3$ pivots, and therefore the number of pivot columns is $3.$

content.problem:
What are the pivot columns of the matrix $P,$ given by

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}7 & 2 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 6\end{aligned}]?
$$
content.worked_solution:
First, we need to convert $P$ to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =[\begin{aligned}7 & 2 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & ↔{R}_{4} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}7 & 2 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Looking at the row echelon form, we see that $P$ has $3$ pivots. In particular, the pivot columns are the $1$st, $2$nd, and $4$th columns.

What are the pivot columns of the matrix $A,$ given by

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 8 & -6 \\ 0 & -2 & -4 & 1 \\ 1 & 4 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]?
$$

$$
